text:
elena: heads-up — SNYK flagged CVE-2026-XXXX in libssl 3.x present in our ubuntu-slim base. low exploitable surface in our containers but we need a preflight plan for rebuilding the slim images and signing them

sam: +1. do we know which images actually include libssl 3.x? slim vs full?

elena: I grepped the runtime layers quickly — ubuntu-slim:22.04 + a couple of internal minimal images pull in libssl3 via curl/ca-certificates in some variants. not all services use that layer but enough to matter (ingest, runner).

mohit: important to check glibc dependency too — renaming openssl symbols broke on older musl variants in the last sweep. multiarch is the trickiest bit (arm64).

qa-jen: what do you want from QA for the preflight? smoke tests, perf baseline, and a regression prompt set?

elena: proposed preflight checklist (quick):
1) Rebuild ubuntu-slim and our internal-minimal with patched libssl/glibc packages.
2) Produce SBOM and attest with cosign.
3) KMS-sign image manifest (customer KMS integration checklist) and store attestation in repo.
4) Canary deploy to two non-prod clusters (us-west + eu-central).
5) Run smoke + auth + token rotation tests, and latency sample.
6) Roll forward if no failures for 24h, otherwise rollback and escalate.

sam: question on step 3 — who owns signer keys? we need an RBAC gating change so only the "image-signer" role can cosign in CI. currently deploy-bot does the push.

mohit: agree. security wants a separate principal for signing with limited IAM perms. propose: create service account image-signer with KMS encrypt/decrypt/sign only on the signing key, and deny push to production registries. ops to handle registry push perms.

elena: I'll file the RBAC ticket. also, any objections to using ephemeral signing keys rotated weekly (short-lived) + a long-lived root that we keep offline for attestation recovery?

sam: ephemeral is good but we must ensure CI can fetch short-lived creds via workload identity. document that flow in the RBAC ticket.

qa-jen: for smoke tests, can we add a quick scripted curl against the internal health endpoints and a small avx/kv sanity check? I'd like to capture traces for any TLS handshake failures.

elena: yes. CI will run:

```bash
# build + sign (CI snippet)
docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 -t registry.redwood/infrabase:slim-patched-$CI_COMMIT \
  --push .
cosign sign --key ksm://projects/rw/keys/image-signer registry.redwood/infrabase:slim-patched-$CI_COMMIT
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot triggered canary build 2177777801 — build succeeded on amd64, arm64 passed but with warnings: "libcrypto: symbol version mismatch" (warning-tag).

mohit: that warning is the usual glibc / musl cross-compat noise. we should gate musl-based images separately. make sure the arm64 variant runs the small CLI smoke test.

qa-jen: ran the smoke suite against canary in staging: TLS handshake failed on 1/10 calls (intermittent). logs:

```
ERROR  tls: handshake failure: remote error: tls: bad certificate
stack: /usr/local/bin/healthcheck: line 42
```

sam: could be that the cert chain in the minimal image is older post-rebuild. Did the CA bundle update?

elena: I rebuilt with distro's latest ca-certificates. but the runtime uses our pinned certs in /opt/certs — QA used the host certs by mistake, investigating.

mohit: while we sort that, we should add an automatic rollback hook if >5% TLS errors over 15m. don't want production user traffic hit with degraded TLS.

elena: agreed. ops, can you add a canary policy?

deploy-bot: added canary policy: rollback if TLS_error_rate > 5% over 15m for route /api/health. Canary window 30m.

ops-bot: also added image attestation check step: registry only promotes images with cosign attestation present and key ID in allowlist.

sam: timeline — can we do staged rebuild + canary today and full rollout tomorrow morning? customers in europe — prefer quieter hours.

elena: timeline works. immediate tasks:
- elena: open RBAC ticket and attach policy snippet
- mohit: verify arm64 musl smoke tests and triage symbol-warning
- qa-jen: expand smoke tests to capture TLS failure traces and record baseline
- ops: enforce cosign attestation gating and add rollback hook

sam: RBAC snippet for image-signer (example IAM):

```json
{
  "principal": "serviceAccount:image-signer@redwood-infra",
  "bindings": [
    {"role": "kms.signer", "resource": "projects/rw/keys/image-signing-key"},
    {"role": "storage.write", "resource": "registry.redwood/images/staging"}
  ]
}
```

elena: thanks — please make the ticket and link CI job. I'll coordinate the canary tomorrow. ping me if QA blocks. :thumbsup:

qa-jen: I'll post a short test report in this thread after the next run.

mohit: if TLS errors persist after cert fix, we should fall back to the previous base image and run binary diff on OpenSSL symbols to see if ABI changed.

elena: agreed. fallback plan documented in the RBAC ticket.

ops-bot: note: remember to update SBOM and attach to release notes so SOC can verify patching for compliance audit.

elena: copy. closing the loop here — I'll send the RBAC + attestation ticket link in an update. thanks all.
